The '''2008–09 Scottish Premier League''' season was the eleventh season of the [[Scottish Premier League]] and the second season under the sponsorship of the [[Clydesdale Bank]]. It began on 9 August 2008 with a game between [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]] and [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/scot_prem/7548329.stm|title=Falkirk 0-1 Rangers |date=9 August 2008|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=26 May 2009}}</ref> After the 33rd round of matches, the league split in half and each team played a further five matches against the teams in their half of the league.

For the second season in succession, the championship was determined on the final day of the season. Leaders Rangers travelled to [[Tannadice Park|Tannadice]] to play [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]] knowing that a win would secure the title. Meanwhile, [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] needed to win their final match of the season against [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Hearts]] at [[Celtic Park]] and hope that Rangers failed to win to retain the title. In the end, Rangers won 3–0 with goals by [[Kyle Lafferty]], [[Pedro Mendes (footballer, born 1979)|Pedro Mendes]] and the league's top goalscorer, [[Kris Boyd]], clinching their first title in four years.<ref name=":0">{{cite web|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/scot_prem/8062744.stm|title=Dundee United 0-3 Rangers|date=24 May 2009|publisher=BBC Sport |access-date=26 May 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090527103957/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/scot_prem/8062744.stm|archive-date=27 May 2009|url-status=live 
}}</ref> Meanwhile, Celtic and Hearts drew 0-0.<ref name=":0" />

Rangers qualified directly for the [[UEFA Champions League 2009–10|Champions League]], while second-placed Celtic qualified for the [[UEFA Champions League 2009–10|qualifying rounds]]. Four teams qualified for the new [[Europa League]]: Hearts and [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]] via league position, [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]] via the [[Scottish Cup]], and [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]] by the Fair Play initiative. [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness]] were [[promotion and relegation|relegated]] after their fifth season in the SPL and were replaced by [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]] for the [[2009–10 Scottish Premier League|following season's competition]].

==Events==
{{main|2008–09 in Scottish football#Notable events}}

* 8 August – Former SPL members and [[Scottish Cup]] finalists [[Gretna F.C.|Gretna]] are formally liquidated by the club's administrators<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.cumberland-news.co.uk/1.218555 |title=Liquidation signals the final nail in Gretna coffin |work=The Cumberland News |date=8 August 2008 |access-date=14 March 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090314001628/http://www.cumberland-news.co.uk/1.218555 |archive-date=14 March 2009 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
* 3 January – [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]] drew 0–0 with [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]] in their last game at [[Love Street (stadium)|Love Street]] before they moved to [[New St Mirren Park]]<ref>{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/scot_prem/7806021.stm|title=St Mirren 0-0 Motherwell |date=3 January 2008|publisher=[[BBC Sport]]|access-date=9 January 2008}}</ref>
* 31 January – St Mirren drew 1–1 with [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]] in their first match at their new stadium<ref>{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/scot_prem/7858986.stm|title=St Mirren 1-1 Kilmarnock |date=31 January 2009|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=1 March 2009| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20090203125954/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/scot_prem/7858986.stm| archive-date= 3 February 2009 | url-status= live}}</ref>
* 2 May – [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]] won promotion to the [[Scottish Premier League]] as [[Scottish First Division|First Division]] champions following a 3–1 win over [[Greenock Morton F.C.|Greenock Morton]]<ref>{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/scot_div_1/8028043.stm|publisher=BBC Sport|title=St Johnstone 3–1 Morton |date=2 May 2009|access-date=3 May 2009| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20090504072854/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/scot_div_1/8028043.stm| archive-date= 4 May 2009 | url-status= live}}</ref>
*23 May – [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]] were relegated after losing 1–0 to [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]] at the [[Caledonian Stadium]]<ref>{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/scot_prem/8062736.stm|publisher=BBC Sport|title= Inverness CT 0-1 Falkirk|date=23 May 2009|access-date=23 May 2009| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20090525155559/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/scot_prem/8062736.stm| archive-date=25 May 2009| url-status= live}}</ref>
